ai.title: Add hot reloading for local agents
ai.summary: Local agent loading switched from dynamic `import()` to `require()` with cache invalidation (`delete require.cache[fullPath]`) to enable hot reloading of `.agents` files. `npm-app/src/agents/load-agents.ts` implements this mechanism, while `npm-app/src/client.ts` integrates `loadLocalAgents` into session initialization. `npm-app/src/cli.ts` refactors user input forwarding to use `this.forwardUserInput`. `.agents/brainstormer.ts` updated to use `import type` for `AgentConfig`.

eli5.text: When you're building an agent locally (in.agents files), any edits you make to that file are now picked up immediately without restarting the process you're running. The system now loads these local agents differently under the hood in a way that actively clears old cached versions each time the agent is needed, keeping your session in sync with the file as you change it. This affects developers building custom agents locally and who would notice that changes to their.agents file take effect without requiring a manual restart.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to read and check your custom assistant templates, it now does the checking directly in one quick step instead of setting up a separate tracking object that remembers previous results. You won't see any difference in what gets built, but the behind-the-scenes checking used to rely on a stateful service that loaded templates asynchronously; that service is gone, replaced by a single synchronous function that both the main backend and the web publish-endpoint now call. This means validation errors and converted templates come back together in one pass, with no lingering service state carried between calls.

ai.summary: CodebuffMessageSchema gains optional keepDuringTruncation boolean. trimMessagesToFitTokenLimit now calculates required tokens for flagged messages first, then removes unflagged messages to fit the remaining budget, replacing removed blocks with 'Previous message(s) omitted due to length'. run-agent-step.ts sets keepDuringTruncation: true for user prompts, instructions, and step prompts, while defaulting history to false. eli5.text: Publishers, creators who distribute content through the system, can now be owned by an organization as well as by an individual. If you create a publisher, the record no longer requires a personal owner; instead it tracks which individual created it and optionally links it to the organization, so a team can jointly maintain the publisher while a specific person is credited as the creator. The old rule tying every publisher to one person has been removed, and new publisher accounts accept an optional organization, with the creator always specified.

ai.title: Refactor agent template registry and resolution
ai.summary: Agent template resolution shifted from a global `agentRegistry` to localized `localAgentTemplates` passed via options, removing dynamic imports and circular dependency risks. The `agent-registry.ts` file now implements a database-backed cache for remote agents alongside static templates, parsing IDs as `publisher/agent@version`. `mainPrompt` and `runAgentStep` were updated to accept `localAgentTemplates` directly, eliminating the need for `getAllAgentTemplates` calls in hot paths.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to decide who should handle a task, it now uses a pre-packaged set of instructions that travel with each session instead of looking them up in a shared global list. This means agent templates (the predefined roles and prompts) are bundled locally per session via 'localAgentTemplates', passed directly through the options of mainPrompt and runAgentStep, rather than fetched dynamically through getAllAgentTemplates calls. The result is faster startup and no risk of circular dependencies or stale global state affecting agent behavior mid-run. You, as the reader, would notice nothing directly unless you were looking at logs or timing: sessions launch a bit quicker and template resolution is more predictable.

ai.title: Reorder agent config types and update changes-reviewer
ai.summary: Refactored `agent-config.d.ts` by moving prompt fields (`parentPrompt`, `systemPrompt`, etc.) out of the core `AgentConfig` interface and reordering type definitions in `tools.d.ts`. Updated `.agents/changes-reviewer.ts` to align with new config structure, explicitly setting `includeMessageHistory: false` and reordering instructions. Scope covers shared core types and the internal changes-reviewer agent. No user-facing behavior changes; purely internal type hygiene and config alignment.

eli5.text: This change is behind-the-scenes cleanup with no visible effect on how anything works. The developers reorganized how the code that guides the software's assistant agents is structured and updated documentation that tells those assistants how to behave, but the actual actions the assistants take stay the same. If you looked at the files, you'd see the instructions got tidied into bullet points and a setting that controls whether past conversations are kept was explicitly set to be turned off. It's already live today, but only affects how the internal team writes and maintains the agent instructions, not what the agents do for you.

ai.title: publish.ts sends authToken in body instead of Cookie header
ai.summary: The `publishAgentTemplate` function in `npm-app/src/cli-handlers/publish.ts` now includes `authToken` in the POST request body, replacing the previous `Cookie` header approach. This change aligns with backend expectations for authentication data placement. The update affects the CLI publish handler for agent templates.

eli5.text: When you publish an assistant template using the command-line tool, the software now sends your login token as part of the message body instead of sticking it in a separate header. This is the kind of behind-the-scenes tweak that keeps things working smoothly with the system that receives the template, so you won't notice any difference in how publishing works on your end. The change is already live today for anyone using the CLI to publish templates.

ai.title: Add backend agent configs to .agents directory
ai.summary: New agent configuration files added to `.agents/` for `ask`, `base-experimental`, `base-lite`, and others. These define models (e.g., `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05`), tool sets, and system prompts for backend orchestration. Updates `backend/src/templates/agent-list.ts` and `common/src/types/session-state.ts` to register these agents. Excludes agent builder per notes.

eli5.text: The system now saves the settings for each helper assistant in a dedicated folder, so the main assistant can tell them apart and hand off the right job to the right helper. You as a user won't see a new button or menu, but if you peek at the code you would spot 12 new files living in a.agents/ folder, each spelling out how one helper should chat, which model to trust, and what tools it can reach for. The main assistant also got an updated address book that lists these helpers, so starting today the project is wired to keep them organized even if nothing behaves differently on the surface.

ai.title: Agent page shows full ID with copy button
ai.summary: Agent detail page now displays the full `publisher/agent@version` ID alongside an `EnhancedCopyButton`. The version is derived by sorting `allVersions` by `created_at` descending. This replaces the previous partial ID display and adds a `pointer-events-none` style to the version badge to prevent interaction conflicts.

eli5.text: When you view a specific version of an agent on its detail page, you can now see the full agent identifier, a complete address made up of the publisher name, agent name, and its version, all in one line. Next to that full identifier is a copy button so you can grab the entire ID and paste it elsewhere without retyping it. The version shown is always the most recently created one, and the small version tags next to older versions are now styled so they can't be accidentally clicked, keeping the page cleaner and easier to use.

ai.title: agents/publish API adds cookie then token auth fallback
ai.summary: web/src/app/api/agents/publish/route.ts now checks session cookie first, then falls back to checkAuthToken({ authToken }) on request body authToken. Previously cookie-only; CLI or non-browser publishers hitting 401 could not publish. Scope: web API route only. authToken is required field in publishAgentRequestSchema, validated via checkAuthToken from @codebuff/internal; 401 returned if both cookie and token fail.

eli5.text: The agent publishing tool now lets you log in two ways: with your normal web session cookie, or with an auth token in the request body. If your browser session is recognized, it uses that; if not, it checks the token you provide, and only rejects the request if neither works. You'd notice this if you're using a script, CLI, or other non-browser tool to publish agents: previously those requests got a 401 error even with a valid token, and now they can authenticate successfully using the token when the cookie isn't present.

eli5.text: The people who check that the assistant behaves correctly swapped a few typed-in shortcut names for the official nicknames pulled straight from the master list, so the helper tools now watch exactly the same names the real program uses instead of their own handwritten copies. While testing how the assistant greets its helper tools, they also quietly fixed one name that had been misspelled the whole time. Nothing changes what you see from day to day, but if something ever breaks, it is easier to spot because the tests now match the real naming rules.

eli5.text: The software you use has been updated to a new release version (1.0.449) that contains several small but helpful improvements. Most noticeably, when you view an agent's details, the full identifier (like publisher/agent@version) is now displayed prominently, and you can click a button to copy it to your clipboard instead of having to manually select and copy the text. The agent publishing system also became more reliable by sending authentication tokens in the request body rather than through cookies, which makes it work better across different network setups. Behind the scenes, the way agent configurations are organized and tested has been cleaned up to make the system more stable and easier to maintain going forward. This update is live now, so these changes are active whenever you use the software today.

ai.title: Agent registry loads DB agents with versioned IDs and validation
ai.summary: fetchAgentFromDatabase in backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts now accepts a parsed ID object, treats 'latest' as a version wildcard, and stamps loaded agents with publisher/agent-id@version before passing them through validateSingleAgent. common/src/templates/agent-validation.ts drops its outer try/catch, moves collectAgentIds and duplicate-ID detection into validateAgents, and switches validateSingleAgent to an options-object signature. common/src/templates/dynamic-agent-functions.ts is a new file exporting collectAgentIds and validateAgents for standalone dynamic-template loading. Validation failures log via logger.error and return null, so invalid DB agents are skipped instead of crashing the registry.

eli5.text: If you ask the system to load an AI assistant that lives in the database, it now handles version labels like 'latest' correctly, checks that the assistant is valid, and quietly skips any that are broken instead of stopping everything. When building a collection of assistants, it first gathers all their names so it can spot duplicates, then validates each one and reports failures by logging them and returning nothing, rather than crashing. This behavior is live today, so any assistant loaded from the database now passes through these safer checks automatically.
